objective: Out-of-sample test of Goldstein-Li-Wang (2026) on the 2026 US midterm control markets: same transformation, assets and directions, a different election, with costs, a shift gate and placebos.

sources.core_claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026-09-03): in Polymarket 2024-01-05..2024-11-05 a one-percentage-point rise in the Trump-win probability goes with 13 bp of next-day return of Trump trades (pooled), and a probability-based strategy shows an annualised Sharpe of 1.95 over April-November 2024; the authors state the statistics are in-sample and gross of transaction costs.
sources.project_applicability: The claim under out-of-sample test: same mechanism, same transformation, same assets and directions, a different election and period.
sources.reflection: The claim under test; no costs, one event.

sources.core_claim: Goldstein, Li and Wang (2026) build the strategy signal by a 5-day EMA of the daily change in the Trump-win probability, a 60-day rolling percentile rank, and a linear map to [-1, 1]; returns are equal-weighted averages across the assets, evaluation from April 1 to the election day after a 60-session burn-in.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the frozen transformation of hypotheses.md.
sources.reflection: Implemented exactly; two unstated conventions fixed in the design.

sources.core_claim: Internet Appendix Table A.1 of the Goldstein-Li-Wang paper (included in the snapshot after the main text) gives the asset directions: all ten stock ETFs, the six banks, UUP and the three connected stocks are long a higher Trump probability, the seven Treasury ETFs are short; this matches the fallback directions frozen in hypotheses.md.
sources.project_applicability: Directions used verbatim; the frozen fallback was not needed.
sources.reflection: Directions taken verbatim; assumption that Republican Congress control carries the Trump-win exposure.

sources.core_claim: SECONDARY (news article, WebFetch extraction): Citigroup argues that a Democratic Congress facing a Republican president means gridlock that bond markets like, tying Polymarket midterm control odds to Treasury yields; same sign as the frozen direction of bonds short a higher Republican probability.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the economic sign of the bond leg only; no number enters the design.
sources.reflection: Supports only the sign of the bond leg.

sources.core_claim: Polymarket Gamma lists the events Which party will win the House in 2026 (id 32225) and Senate (id 32224), both created 2025-07-11 and ending 2026-11-04, each with separate Democratic and Republican Yes/No markets and CLOB token ids; both are unresolved on 2026-10-04.
sources.project_applicability: Defines the signal markets and the Republican Yes tokens.
sources.reflection: Defines the signal markets and tokens.

sources.core_claim: Kalshi lists CONTROLH-2026 and CONTROLS-2026 with Democratic and Republican markets open since 2024-11-06 (public candlestick endpoint, no key); used only as the robustness signal.

The public CLOB /prices-history endpoint returns timestamped prices for a resolved market (daily points for fidelity 1440 in the probe); the intel notes record that hourly and finer history needs startTs/endTs windows and that interval=max with fidelity 60 returned empty.
sources.project_applicability: Data source for the daily 4 pm probabilities of the control markets.
sources.reflection: Hourly windowed history is the data source.

sources.core_claim: Kalshi distributions are accurate forecasts of macro outcomes (for headline CPI a statistically significant improvement over the Bloomberg consensus); the paper tests forecast accuracy and news response, not stock returns.
sources.project_applicability: Shows regulated event-contract prices carry real information; motivates the Kalshi robustness signal, no stock-return test.
sources.reflection: Accuracy of regulated event contracts; not a return test.

sources.core_claim: Qin and Yang (arXiv 2606.04217) describe the Polymarket-v1 on-chain trade archive, 2022-11-21 to 2026-04-28, 1.20 billion trades, and show that tick-rule and bulk-volume classifiers are near random on it.
sources.project_applicability: Last prints in thin Polymarket markets are noisy; the daily 16:00 ET price is taken from the last CLOB point and a missing session carries the last price.

sources.core_claim: Leigh, Wolfers and Zitzewitz (NBER w9587, 2003): the price of a prediction-market security on Saddam Hussein's survival moves with spot oil and equity-sector prices, so an event probability can be mapped to asset returns by a stated policy channel; 20-year-old precedent for translating event odds into asset exposures.
sources.project_applicability: Precedent for the mapping of event odds to policy-sensitive assets; no number enters the design.
sources.reflection: Precedent for odds to asset mapping.

candidate_matrix_revisions.effect: Added costs, a 1000-shift gate, a sign-flip placebo and an unrelated-market placebo; the claim is tested on a different election, not extended.
Fixed pandas ewm(span=5, adjust=False) and average-rank percentiles before any return was computed.
Signal is the Republican-control probability of House and Senate; directions kept as in Table A.1 and the mapping stated as the assumption of the test.
Power statement frozen in hypotheses.md (expected t about 1.2 at true Sharpe 1.0); a forward shadow to 2026-11-04 is preregistered.
